newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Tyumen Oil Co sees output slip in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Tyumen Oil Co sees output slip in 1997.

text.p: Russia's Tyumen Oil Company, whose board chairman is former Fuel and Energy Minister Yuri Shafranik, said on Monday that its crude oil output would slip in 1997 to 20.08 million tonnes (around 402,000 barrels per day).
Shafranik, speaking to reporters, forecast the company's 1996 output at 20.53 million tonnes (411,000 bpd), below 1995's 22.57 million (451,000 bpd).
But he said Tyumenskaya Neftyanyaya Kompaniya, one of Russia's 13 vertically-integrated oil companies, had debts of eight trillion roubles.
Seven trillion roubles of the debt were carried by its main operating unit, the Nizhnevartovskneftegaz NZGZ.RTS 0#NZGZ.RUO producer.
Shafranik said Tyumen would announce a plan in 1997 to restructure the producer's debts and to ensure steadier supplies to its Ryazan refinery, which is working far below capacity.
He also said the company, which is nearly 100 percent state-owned, planned to centralise its refined oil products sales.
